items.name: utils
items.title: Utils
items.description: cn() (clsx + tailwind-merge) and the WithElementRef / WithoutChild… type helpers. Every item depends on it.

items.name: motion
items.title: Motion
items.description: The durations and curves the moving items share, as CSS variables: a strong ease-out to land on, and short times. Reduced motion shortens them. The same values as src/app.css.

items.name: activity-graph
items.title: Activity graph
items.description: A contribution graph for habits and routines, GitHub's grid of small rounded squares: one per day, week, month or year, tinted by level. Parts: ActivityGraph (root: `data` keyed YYYY-MM-DD and summed into coarser cells, `granularity` day | week | month | year, optional `range`, required `locale` and `weekStartsOn`, `thresholds` for levels 1-4, bindable `selected`), ActivityGraphRowLabels, ActivityGraphViewport (a sideways scroller, opens at the newest), ActivityGraphColumnLabels, ActivityGraphGrid (ARIA grid with one roving tab stop; renders each cell through a `cell` snippet so the consumer gives words and a Tooltip), ActivityGraphCell (aria-label required), ActivityGraphCaption (optional; turns selection on and shows the selected cell's words, so touch gets the value), ActivityGraphLegend and ActivityGraphLegendScale. Levels: five tonal steps of foreground mixed into muted, distinct in both themes; forced colours keep the fills. No copy, no default locale or week start.

items.name: agent-tree
items.title: Agent tree
items.description: Coding agents as a process tree, with the rules Linux uses: every agent has a pid, a parent and exactly one state (working R, waiting or needs-you S, paused T, done or failed with an exit code); you are process 1 at the top. Selecting an agent shows its reach: what it steers (everything below it, in the one colour) and whom it reports to. Sockets between siblings, opened by a shared ancestor, and two agents in one file show on the rows. Keyboard: arrows move, Enter selects. An `actions` snippet renders the app's own Pause, Stop, Message inside the selected row.

items.name: color-picker
items.title: Color Picker
items.description: One colour out of a few, as a row of swatches, and a hex field for any other: ColorPicker (bits-ui RadioGroup; bind:value is the picked swatch's value as written, name and required for forms, disabled), ColorPickerSwatch (a 32px disc of any CSS colour with a hairline, drawn in with a primary ring when picked, 44px to touch, aria-label required) and ColorPickerInput (hex in a stock Input with a preview of the colour at its start; bind it to the same value and the two follow each other; writes #rrggbb, bind:invalid, Escape puts it back). Tab enters the swatches at the picked one, the arrows move and pick. No copy inside: you name every colour.

items.name: dial
items.title: Dial
items.description: A rotary knob that picks one of a few stops (role=slider). Parts: Dial (the root and the slider element: step as a list of values at equal angles or a number, sweep and start angle, bind:value, wrap, disabled, sizes default and sm), DialKnob (the key with a copper pointer line; it turns, gives a little while held and carries the focus ring), DialStop (one per stop, like a clock face: major a long mark with the consumer's label outside, minor a short mark between; the selected mark is copper) and DialUnit (the unit in the sweep's open gap). Keyboard: arrows a stop, Page Up/Down a tenth, Home/End. Pointer: the stop at the pointer's angle, snapping live, with a light haptic per stop on touch. Only the ring around the knob captures the finger; a vertical swipe on the knob scrolls the page. In a form, name submits the stop it is on and form.reset() puts it back to the mount value. No copy inside: aria-label and aria-valuetext come from the consumer.

items.name: form-reset
items.title: Form reset
items.description: restoreOnReset(el, restore, setDefault?) and hiddenInputOf(el): form reset for controls drawn by bits-ui. bits-ui does not put the drawn control back on form.reset(); restoreOnReset listens for the owning form's reset (the hidden input's form, else the closest form) and calls restore() inside the event, flushed, so the form reads as reset as soon as reset() returns, as with native controls; a cancelled reset is left alone. setDefault puts the mount state on the hidden input (defaultChecked or defaultValue). The component keeps its own mount snapshot. hiddenInputOf finds bits-ui's hidden input (the aria-hidden input right after the root). Switch and Dial use it; no copy, no markup.

items.name: inert-outside
items.title: Inert outside
items.description: inertOutside({ keep }): an attachment for a modal layer's surface. While it is open (data-state="open", or none) every element outside it is inert (not focusable, not clickable, hidden from assistive tech that ignores aria-modal): it walks from the surface up to body and makes each sibling on the way inert, so a surface rendered in place works like one in a portal. What keep matches (default [data-slot=toaster]) and the way up to it stay usable. The page comes back the moment data-state leaves open, before the exit motion, so focus can return. Nested layers make their parent inert and give back only what they took; an element the author made inert is never touched. modalLayers.open counts the open layers (reactive). No copy, no markup.

items.name: middot
items.title: Middot
items.description: The separator between two pieces of meta ("Tomorrow · 09:00"). A drawn dot with exactly the same space on both sides (0.4em), sitting on the middle of the lowercase letters, instead of the "·" character between two narrow font spaces. Carries " · " as visually hidden text so screen readers and copy-paste keep the separation.

items.name: number-input
items.title: Number input
items.description: A number you step with two chevrons or type; the digits roll to the new value with NumberFlow, as an odometer does, so you see what changed and which way. Arrow keys step (Shift: ten steps; Home and End: the bounds), a chevron held keeps stepping, and the field never holds an invalid value: typed text is taken as soon as it reads as a number and clamped when you leave. Formats through Intl.NumberFormat (locale, currency, decimals). AnimatedNumber, the rolling digits, is exported on its own for a counter that only shows.

items.name: scroll-map
items.title: Scroll map
items.description: A slim map beside a long scroll (a conversation or a long document): one tick per turn or section, the ticks in view lifted as a band. Parts: ScrollMap (a <nav>; `target` is the scrolling element, followed so the band tracks the real scroll position; while the map shows it is the only indicator, so the target's scrollbar is hidden and comes back where the map hides; `side` right | left; `scrollMargin`), ScrollMapTicks (the column with the band; one tab stop with ArrowUp / ArrowDown / Home / End), ScrollMapTick (size default or sm, `dot` for a section with attachments; hover or focus shows a Tooltip with ScrollMapTickTitle and ScrollMapTickDescription; press or Enter jumps there; `value` is an element id), ScrollMapPrevious / ScrollMapNext (ghost icon buttons). For a pointer and room: it hides itself at a coarse primary pointer (phones, touch tablets); leave it out in a narrow column. No copy inside; the nav, ticks and buttons require aria-labels.

items.name: stepper
items.title: Stepper
items.description: A task in a few ordered steps (account setup, checkout). Parts: Stepper (bind:value = the current step from 1; horizontal | vertical; linear by default: back to any earlier step, ahead only past done steps; or free), StepperList (default, or the inline bars | dots), StepperItem (value, done (default: before the furthest step reached), disabled, loading, invalid), StepperTrigger, StepperIndicator (a ring, a copper disc when active, a tonal disc with a check when done; a Spinner while loading, a red ring with an X when invalid), StepperTitle, StepperDescription, StepperSeparator (a foreground fill that scales in once the current step lies past it, and out when you go back), StepperContent and StepperPrevious / StepperNext (stock Buttons, dimmed but focusable at the ends). In a form, StepperNext checks the current panel's fields first, and a submit with an invalid hidden field goes to its step. Keyboard: the triggers share one tab stop, arrows move, Enter / Space go. Under 30rem only the current title stays in sight.

items.name: swap
items.title: Swap
items.description: Several things on one spot, one shown at a time (Swap + SwapItem active): an icon and its label turning into a check and "Copied", a play icon into pause. The items share one grid cell, so the box keeps the width of the widest and nothing moves. The change is Emil Kowalski's icon swap: both at once, a 4px blur cross-fade on base 220ms (ease-out), icons shrinking to and growing from 25%, words only blurring; reduced motion: a plain fade. Inactive items are hidden from screen readers; announce the change with a live region where it matters.

items.name: swipe
items.title: Swipe
items.description: The physics of a swipe, shared by SwipeDeck and the Toaster; the caller passes every number. rubber(d, max): the asymptotic give of a side that cannot be pulled. VelocityTracker(window): push(t, x, y) per move, velocity(at, stale) on release in px/ms, zero after a rest of `stale` ms. exitDuration(dist, speed, quick, base): an ease-out that leaves at the finger's speed, bounded quick to base. SwipeMotion: one rAF motion at a time, tween(duration, ease, frame, done) and spring(read, write, v0, { stiffness, dampingRatio, timeScale }, done) home to 0 on any number of axes. ClickSwallow: arm() after a drag, swallow(event) in onclickcapture, armed until the end of the task. CARD_SWIPE_GESTURE is a swiped card's tuning (slop 8, hysteresis 6, flick 0.5px/ms from 16px, rubber 32, stale 60ms, window 100ms, spring 400 / 0.78), a named preset, never a default. Pointer handling, axes, zones and layout stay in each component. No markup, no copy.

items.name: swipe-deck
items.title: Swipe deck
items.description: A stack of cards you go through one at a time, swiping each away. Parts: SwipeDeck (root, one tab stop), SwipeDeckStack (the stage), SwipeDeckCard (any content as children, `value` is its identity), SwipeDeckLabel (turns `left`, `right` or `up` on for its card; an icon in a circle over the card that grows with the drag, in its button's colour: `variant` outline or default; its word is announced), SwipeDeckEmpty (shown once no card is left), SwipeDeckActions with SwipeDeckAction (a Button per direction) and SwipeDeckUndo. The drag locks to an axis, follows 1:1 toward a labelled direction, rubber-bands elsewhere, commits past a threshold or on a flick, else springs home. The deck owns the order and a 10-step history: onSwipe(card, direction, { via }) fires as a card leaves (return false to keep it); undo (button, Backspace, Cmd+Z / Ctrl+Z, undo()) brings it back and calls onUndo. Keyboard: Left, Right, Up; the label is announced. Only a dragged card has a shadow. Reduced motion cross-fades. No copy inside.

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.description: A switch on bits-ui Switch, with the part name of the stock shadcn-svelte Switch, for settings that apply at once. The knob is the one moving piece: it slides on settle while the colour of the state it goes to is wiped in behind it (copper from the start, the track from the end), and holding stretches the knob toward its destination. Sizes default (52 × 32) and sm (40 × 24), both 44px to touch. In a form, with a name, it always submits: value ("on") while on, uncheckedValue ("off") while off; disabled, nothing. form.reset() puts it back to its mount state, drawn and submitted alike. bind:checked may point at an undefined value (a missing record key): it reads as off.

items.name: tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.description: A segmented control on bits-ui Tabs, with the part names of stock shadcn-svelte Tabs. The selected segment carries one moving piece, a key on a pill track; the segments themselves are flat labels. The key and its foreground labels are one clip-path layer that slides between segments, so the label colour and the key move in step. The panel follows the key: TabsContent comes in 8px from the side the selection moved to, and a step by keyboard switches at once. An optional tabular count and leading or trailing icons; `mode="radio"` for a single choice without panels (radiogroup / radio). With too many segments for the width, the track scrolls sideways without a scrollbar, the selected segment is scrolled into view, and the edge with more behind it fades where scroll-state container queries exist.

items.name: terminal
items.title: Terminal
items.description: Command output on the muted surface, flat, in both themes. Parts: Terminal (owns `output`, a string with ANSI escapes or an array of lines, and `streaming`), TerminalHeader, TerminalTitle (names the log), TerminalStatus (role=status), TerminalActions, TerminalButton (a ghost icon Button), TerminalCopyButton (copies the text without escapes; `copiedLabel` required), TerminalClearButton (the consumer empties `output`), TerminalContent (a native scrolling box with a role=log inside, aria-busy while streaming; sticks to the bottom while output arrives, lets go when the reader scrolls up; `wrap` or sideways scroll; a block cursor while streaming) and TerminalEmpty. Long logs stay cheap: only the new tail is parsed (parseAnsiIncremental, exported). ansi.ts parses SGR styles and colours (16, 256, truecolour) and strips other escapes; output is spans, never HTML. The 16 colours are the component's own --terminal-* variables, for light and .dark, each at least 4.5:1 on muted.

items.name: textarea
items.title: Textarea
items.description: The multi-line field, with the part name of the stock shadcn-svelte Textarea and the look of the stock Input: 96px tall at least, destructive ring when aria-invalid. The fixed one has its own grip in the bottom-right corner, inside the rounding (the native resizer is hidden): a drag changes the height between the field's min-h and max-h; with resizeLabel it is a focusable separator (arrows a line, Home/End the limits); resizable={false} leaves it out. `autogrow` grows it with its text instead (CSS field-sizing: content, a script fallback elsewhere) up to a max-h you set, without a grip. Native validation rings it once it was left wrong or a submit was tried, and aria-invalid follows.

items.name: time-wheel
items.title: Time wheel
items.description: A time you set by turning a wheel, in two styles: flat, as on iOS (the neighbours shrink and fade), or a drum (the rows sit on a cylinder). Hours and minutes in 24 or 12 hours with an am/pm column, one highlight bar across the columns. Drag, mouse wheel, click a row, or ArrowUp/ArrowDown on a focused column (instant). Wheel is one column on its own, for any list.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: What just happened, with its undo: a floating popover block with one line (Archived · Q3 report), the verb in bold, a ghost action and a tonal wash that drains over the 5s window. Variants set the action's ink and the wash on the same surface: default, notice, news. A failure is a toast with a leading icon in text-destructive. Parts: Toast (owns the clock), ToastMessage, ToastVerb, ToastAction, ToastProgress, and Toaster, which renders a queue as one stack; toast({ verb, title, variant, action, duration, onDismiss }) adds to it from anywhere. Newest in front, older ones stepped back, spread on hover, focus or tap. Swipe down or sideways to dismiss. Windows hold on hover, focus, a held finger or a hidden tab. One polite live region; Alt+T moves focus to the front toast and back. While a modal is open the Toaster stands in the top layer. onDismiss says why: timeout, swipe, action, overflow or dismiss.

items.name: view-change
items.title: View change
items.description: ViewChange: a view arriving from the side its entry sits on. Wrap what changes with its key (a route, a section); on a change the content is re-created and comes in 8px from `from` while it fades in (base 220ms on settle), so the eye reads where it came from: the next section from the right, an earlier one from the left, a page from the sidebar's side. sideOf(order, prev, next) gives the side from the entries' order. Without `from` the content is simply replaced (the first render, a keyboard shortcut: never animated). Reduced motion: a fade. The same motion is built into TabsContent, where the side follows the key.

items.name: voice-meter
items.title: Voice Meter
items.description: A calm live level meter for a voice being recorded: one row of small round dots in currentColor, where the louder moments stretch single dots into short rounded bars, never taller than the meter (`count`, `h-*` and `--voice-meter-dot` / `--voice-meter-gap` size it). Levels are 0..1, newest last, from mutually exclusive sources: `levels` the consumer pushes, an `analyser` it owns, or a `stream` (getUserMedia, which the consumer calls). trackVoiceLevel reads an AnalyserNode or MediaStream with Web Audio and closes what it opened on cleanup; it never stops the stream's tracks. Motion is transform only: the row drifts left one slot per sample. Reduced motion: no growth, no drift; the dots fade in strength with the level. Always aria-hidden: the surrounding UI says what is happening in words.
